segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Priya. I’ve got about 25 minutes before I’m back in the CRM cleaning up quarter-end records, so I want to use this for your seat count and go-live questions.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Works for me. We’re still at 84 seats for launch, but finance asked what happens if we add 12 more in November.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: For 84 seats, annual is $52,920. If you add 12 in November, we prorate through the February 28 renewal, so it’s about $3,150 extra, depending on the exact start date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And the invoice, can that be split by department? Our ops team takes 50 seats and support takes 34.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can do two invoice lines under the same contract. Sorry the pricing sheet came over late yesterday; I spent the morning re-keying account data in the billing tool, but the totals on that sheet are current.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: No problem. Legal had one note on the auto-renewal. They want 60 days’ notice instead of 30.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That’s usually fine for a 12-month term. I’ll mark 60 days in the order form and send the redline back today.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. Our target go-live is September 16. Is onboarding still four weeks?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, if we have signature by August 12, we can start kickoff on August 19 and hit September 16. If we can wrap by 2:40, I need to assemble the approval packet for deal desk, then I’ll get you the final version.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That timing works. Send the final order form with 84 seats, split invoice lines, 60-day notice, and the September 16 go-live called out.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send it by end of day, and if finance needs the prorated add-on example in writing, I’ll include that as a note.
